question_text: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
passage_text: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • In 1859, the novel Adam Bede was published in England. • According to the novel’s title page, the author’s name was George Eliot. • George Eliot was widely assumed to be a pseudonym. • A pseudonym is a fake name used to conceal an author’s identity. • A woman named Mary Ann Evans later revealed herself as the novel’s real author. The student wants to identify the real author of Adam Bede.

classification.classification_rationale: This is a grammar-adjacent Expression of Ideas question requiring synthesis of bulleted notes to fulfill a rhetorical goal (identifying the real author). The correct answer must precisely name Mary Ann Evans, not just refer to 'a woman' or repeat the pseudonym. Grammar focus is on precision word choice — selecting the option that most accurately and completely conveys the required information without redundancy or vagueness.

explanation.short: Option A directly identifies Mary Ann Evans as the real author, which fulfills the student's goal using the most relevant and complete information from the notes.
explanation.full: The student’s goal is to identify the real author of Adam Bede. The notes state that George Eliot was the name on the title page, but it was widely assumed to be a pseudonym, and that Mary Ann Evans later revealed herself as the real author. Option A synthesizes these key facts into a single clear statement that directly answers the goal. Option B focuses on the assumption about the pseudonym without identifying the real author. Option C only states what the title page said, not the actual author. Option D is vague — it mentions 'a woman' and 'later revealed' but does not name Mary Ann Evans, making it less precise and effective for the stated goal.

options.label: A
options.text: The real author of Adam Bede was Mary Ann Evans, who published the novel using the pseudonym George Eliot.
options.why_plausible: Directly names Mary Ann Evans and connects her to the pseudonym George Eliot, fulfilling the goal with precise, complete information from the notes.

options.label: B
options.text: George Eliot, which Adam Bede’s title page indicated was the name of the novel’s author, was widely assumed to be a pseudonym.
options.why_wrong: Fails to identify the real author (Mary Ann Evans), instead focusing on the assumption about the pseudonym. Does not accomplish the student’s stated goal.
options.why_plausible: Uses exact phrases from the notes ('title page', 'widely assumed to be a pseudonym') and addresses the pseudonym issue, which is related to the goal.

options.label: C
options.text: The title page of the novel Adam Bede indicated that the author’s name was George Eliot.
options.why_wrong: Only reports what the title page said, not who the real author is. Ignores the key note revealing Mary Ann Evans as the real author.
options.why_plausible: Directly quotes the note about the title page, making it seem factual and relevant.

options.label: D
options.text: A woman who had used a pseudonym to conceal her identity later revealed herself as the real author of Adam Bede.
options.why_wrong: Is imprecise — fails to name Mary Ann Evans, which is essential for identifying the real author. Vague phrasing undermines effectiveness for the specific goal.
options.why_plausible: Mentions 'a woman' and 'revealed herself as the real author,' which aligns with the final note and seems to address the goal.

question_text: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
passage_text: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • The ancient Arab dhow was a sailing vessel distinguishable by its triangular sails and stitched hull construction. • Dhows were used primarily for trade along the coasts of Arab, South Asian, and East African countries. • Contemporary shipbuilders in Oman use a mix of modern and traditional materials to build replicas of ancient dhows. • Most of the materials used are traditional. • Replica hulls are stitched together using the same traditional coconut palm fiber rope used on the hulls of ancient dhows. The student wants to make a generalization about the materials used in dhow replicas.

classification.classification_rationale: This is an Expression of Ideas question requiring synthesis of note content to achieve a rhetorical goal (generalization). It tests precision in word choice to reflect nuanced information ('mix of modern and traditional' vs. 'mostly traditional'). Grammar rules apply because the correct answer must accurately represent the relationship between ideas in the notes without overgeneralizing or omitting key qualifiers.

explanation.short: Option C correctly synthesizes the key point that while most materials are traditional, some modern materials are also used — directly addressing the student’s goal to generalize about materials in dhow replicas.
explanation.full: The student’s goal is to make a generalization about the materials used in dhow replicas. The notes state that contemporary shipbuilders use 'a mix of modern and traditional materials' and that 'most of the materials used are traditional.' Option C captures this nuance by stating, 'Although most materials used in dhow replicas are traditional, some modern materials are used,' which accurately reflects the synthesis of these two facts. Other options either focus on historical features (A, B, D) or fail to address the material composition specifically.

options.label: A
options.text: A traditional material that was used to stitch together the hulls of ancient dhows, coconut palm fiber rope is still used by shipbuilders.
options.why_wrong: Focuses narrowly on one specific material rather than making a generalization about materials overall; fails to address the mix of modern and traditional materials mentioned in the notes.
options.why_plausible: Mentions coconut palm fiber rope, which is noted as a traditional material still used — aligns with part of the notes.

options.label: B
options.text: The ancient Arab dhow was a sailing vessel used primarily for trade and distinguishable by its triangular sails.
options.why_wrong: Describes historical characteristics of ancient dhows, not materials used in modern replicas — completely misses the rhetorical goal.
options.why_plausible: Repeats factual details from the notes about ancient dhows, creating surface familiarity.

options.label: C
options.text: Although most materials used in dhow replicas are traditional, some modern materials are used.
options.why_plausible: Directly synthesizes the two key notes: 'use a mix of modern and traditional materials' and 'most of the materials used are traditional.'

options.label: D
options.text: Contemporary shipbuilders in Oman build replicas of the dhow, which was an ancient sailing vessel with a stitched hull construction.
options.why_wrong: Describes what is being built and historical features, but omits any mention of materials — fails to address the student’s goal to generalize about materials.
options.why_plausible: Includes 'contemporary shipbuilders' and 'replicas,' matching keywords from the notes.
